b.x: ⚠️ Primeiro: A Verdade sobre "Reset Mundial" Não existe uma definição científica única de "reset mundial". Não existe fórmula matemática exata porque estamos lidando com probabilidades subjetivas baseadas em dados incompletos, não com leis da física. O que podemos fazer é usar estimativas de especialistas e cálculos probabilísticos transparentes. 📌 Definições que usarei: - Reset Global Existencial: Colapso civilização em escala mundial — perda irreversível de capacidade tecnológica/industrial; morte de grande parte da população; retorno a sociedades pré-industriais ou pior - Caos Regional/Parcial: Colapso ou instabilidade severa em regiões ou países, mas sem fim da civilização global - Período analisado: 2026 → 2077 = 51 anos 📐 A Matemática — Cálculo Passo a Passo Usamos a fórmula de probabilidade cumulativa para eventos independentes: P(sobrevivência total) = (1 − p₁) × (1 − p₂) × (1 − p₃) × ... P(evento em 51 anos) = 1 − P(sobrevivência total) Isso significa: a chance de NENHUM desastre acontecer é o produto das chances de cada um NÃO acontecer. Subtraímos de 1 para saber a chance de PELO MENOS UM acontecer. 📋 Os Riscos — Estimativas e Cálculos Baseado em pesquisas do Future of Humanity Institute (Oxford), Toby Ord (The Precipice), Fórum Econômico Mundial e outras fontes: Tipo de Reset | Prob. anual estimada | Prob. NÃO acontecer em 51 anos | Prob. DE acontecer até 2077 Guerra Nuclear Global | 0,3% ao ano | (0,997)⁵¹ = 85,7% | 14,3% Mudança Climática Catastrófica | 0,2% ao ano | (0,998)⁵¹ = 90,3% | 9,7% Pandemia (natural ou laboratorial) | 0,15% ao ano | (0,9985)⁵¹ = 92,5% | 7,5% IA descontrolada / Tecnologia perigosa | 0,1% ao ano | (0,999)⁵¹ = 95,0% | 5,0% Impacto de asteroide / Supervulcão | 0,0001% ao ano | ~100% | ≈0,005% Colapso sistêmico (econômico/ecológico) | 0,25% ao ano | (0,9975)⁵¹ = 87,9% | 12,1% 🧮 CÁLCULO FINAL — Reset Mundial Global Passo 1 — Probabilidade de NENHUM risco acontecer: Passo 2 — Probabilidade de ALGUM reset global acontecer até 2077: ≈ 40% de chance de um evento catastrófico global até 2077 🇧🇷 E o Caos Regional / no Brasil? Isso é muito mais provável, pois não exige que o mundo inteiro caia. Inclui instabilidade política, crises econômicas, desastres naturais severos, conflitos locais, colapso de serviços em algumas regiões: Cenário | Chance estimada até 2077 Algum tipo de caos em ALGUM lugar do mundo | 70–85% Instabilidade severa em pelo menos uma região grande | 55–65% Brasil enfrentando crises graves/colapso parcial | 30–45% Brasil completamente colapsado | 5–15% 🔝 Quais são os MAIORES perigos? (Ranking) 1. Guerra Nuclear / Conflito Global — ~14% → O risco mais citado por especialistas 2. Colapso sistêmico combinado (clima + economia + sociedade) — ~12% → Muitos especialistas consideram o mais provável de todos 3. Mudança Climática extremamente grave — ~10% → Risco que cresce com o tempo 4. Pandemia grave (biotecnologia) — ~7,5% → Risco crescente com avanço da ciência 5. Tecnologia (IA/nanotecnologia) — ~5% → Incerteza muito alta 6. Riscos naturais (asteroide, supervulcão) — ~0,005% → Extremamente improvável ⚠️ IMPORTANTÍSSIMO — Limitações desses números "Não são fatos, são estimativas de especialistas." - Toby Ord estima 16% de risco existencial neste século; outros dizem 19%; outros muito menos - O modelo supõe independência entre riscos — na realidade, um risco pode piorar outro (ex: clima piora → conflitos aumentam → risco de guerra sobe) - Fatores humanos, cooperação internacional e tecnologia podem reduzir esses números significativamente - NÃO é uma profecia. É uma faixa de possibilidades baseada no conhecimento atual 📊 Resumo em uma frase: ~40% de chance de algum evento grave em escala global até 2077; ~30–45% de chance de o Brasil enfrentar crises sérias; mas NÃO é inevitável — a chance de NÃO acontecer é maior que a de acontecer.

World reset protocol. Thirty days of total blackout. Premise: no electricity, no internet, no digital communication, no resupply of any kind. People depend only on what exists at moment zero. The numbers below are a scenario, built on urban stock, on how long systems hold, and on how collapse usually moves. It is not the forecast of a date. Day zero. The instant. Midnight: total blackout. The grids fall at the same time. One minute: the traffic lights go out. Traffic locks. Five minutes: the phone loses the signal. The tower has no power. Its backup battery lasts four to eight hours. Thirty minutes: the water pumps stop. The reservoir starts to empty. One hour: payment dies. No instant transfer, no card, no cash machine. The head still says: it will be back in a few hours. Discomfort becomes confusion. Day one. It is not panic yet. From morning to noon, piped water still runs from what is in the tank. The city tower empties in twelve to twenty-four hours. The supermarket fills. Bottled water is gone in the first six to twelve hours. At noon, the station stops pumping. Without electricity, the pump does not turn. Whoever has a full tank still moves. At six, the home refrigerator no longer holds. What spoils starts to go. With the door shut, the safe margin is short, about four hours. At ten, the first night without street light. Dark. A silence the city does not know. On this day, near ninety percent of the water still comes from the tap. About three quarters of the shelves still have something. Gasoline is in the tanks, of cars and of stations, but the station does not deliver it. The car runs while the tank lasts. Day two. Reality shows. In the morning, a line at the station that still has a generator. That ends in hours. At noon, the shelf empties. Bread, milk, and what is fresh are gone in twenty-four to forty-eight hours. In the afternoon, water pressure falls. A tall building no longer has a tap. At night, the bank does not open. Digital money does not exist. Only cash, and there is little of it. About sixty percent of the cars have already stopped, because they cannot refuel. The truck sits on the road. There is no delivery. On this day, about forty percent of the city still has a minimum pressure. At the market, about thirty percent remains, what nobody wanted. Usable gasoline: about five percent, a generator and a full tank. About forty percent still moves, with no resupply. Day three. The turn. Before dawn, the hospital generator starts to die. Diesel is short, and no more is coming. In the morning, piped water has stopped in about eighty percent of the city. At noon, the supermarket is empty. The shelf is clean in forty-eight to seventy-two hours of panic. In the afternoon, looting is no longer shopping. It is need. There is not enough police for all of it. At night, there is no public transport. Subway, train, and bus stopped. The big city starts to break into neighborhoods. Water: under fifteen percent, the tank and the reserve of whoever stored it. Food at the market: none. What exists is inside houses. Gasoline: under one percent, whoever stored it or left with a full tank. Transport stopped. The foot is the means. From day four to day seven. The first week. Day four: a dry tap. No food resupply. What is left in tanks. Sewage comes back, because the pumping station stops in about forty-eight hours. Day five: only the source that does not depend on the grid. The house stock is already falling. Most gasoline is gone. There is no communication. A radio without a battery is silent too. Day six: the neighborhood with a well has the advantage. The refrigerator died, and what was fresh spoiled. Trash in the street, no collection. Day seven: water with sediment and contamination. What remains of food is what keeps. A hospital with no slack. Care, when it exists, is the basic kind. A big city depends on water that comes from outside. It is the most fragile. A farm with its own well crosses better. A city that lives on same-day delivery holds about three days of food. Without resupply, it ends in seventy-two hours. Without sewage treatment, waterborne disease shows at the end of the week. Week two. Hunger and thirst. From day eight to day ten, water is what is worth most. Three liters a person a day is the minimum, not the comfort. From day ten to day fourteen, what spoils is gone in about ninety percent of houses. What does not spoil remains. From day twelve to day fourteen, whoever is in the big city starts walking toward the country, on foot, in groups. The avenue becomes a corridor. On day fourteen, bank money does not buy. Trade is the economy: water, food, shelter, care. An adult, to hold, asks about two thousand calories a day. A house with an ordinary stock has seven to fourteen days of food, if it does not resupply. Without water, in the heat, the limit is about three days. Porto Alegre in the heat tightens that. Week three. The house is rearranged by force. From day fifteen to day twenty, whoever stayed in the city rations for real. A garden in the yard and in the square appears. From day eighteen to day twenty-two, groups harden. Some help. Others take. Territory appears without a written law. On day twenty-one, most medicine that needs cold loses its strength. Insulin, vaccine, some antibiotics. From day twenty-two to day twenty-five, where water is scarce and dirty, diarrhea, chest infection, and a wound that will not close spread. Day thirty. What remained. The big city is emptier. Many left. Others did not cross. A quiet street. The food that exists was planted or was stored. The market does not reopen. What the surroundings produce is what there is. Whoever has a clean source has the life of the street. What is worth flips: a practical skill is worth more than a note. Knowing how to do it is the resource. The light did not return. What broke does not stand up in days. It takes months, and it can take years. The account of the collapse, in this scenario. Piped water: near ninety percent on day one, under five percent on day seven, none on day thirty. It runs out in twenty-four to seventy-two hours. Food at the market: about three quarters on day one, none on day seven, none on day thirty. It runs out in forty-eight to seventy-two hours. Usable gasoline: what is in the tanks on day one, about one percent on day seven, none on day thirty. An ordinary tank ends in three to five days. Digital communication: falls to zero in twenty-four hours. The tower battery lasts four to eight. On day seven and on day thirty, zero. The bank: it works until day two. After that, dead. Without power, the fall is immediate. The lesson of the scenario. No modern system was made to last more than seventy-two hours without electricity. The fall is not slow. It is a cascade. One system falls and takes the next. Whoever leaves on day one or day two has an advantage of account. Whoever hesitates until day three is already inside a system that stopped.
